full_judgment: 18. In a proceeding under section 145 of the Code of Criminal Procedure the learned Magistrate is the competent authority to pass such order about to maintain peace in a property as sought for where there has been any presumption of a breach of peace. The Magistrate after holding an inquiry as well as taking evidence thereto can pass such order, if he found that there is a sufficient cause of breach of peace in the disputed property. It reveals from the impugned judgment and order dated 23-6-2011 that the learned Additional Chief Judicial Magistrate, Bhola after perusing the inquiry report submitted by the concern police station on 10-7-1973 and also evaluating the evidences adduced by the respective parties, in oral and documentary, he passed the said judgment and order on 23-6-2011 allowing the MP Case No. 129 of 1973. After that judgment and order of the learned Magistrate, the learned Sessions Judge, Bhola seating in a revisional jurisdiction under section 439A of the Code of Criminal Procedure he by his judgment and order dated 17-1-2013 in Criminal Revision No. 96 of 2011 after addressing the questions raised before him by the petitioners herein (i.e. the 2nd, 4th and 5th party) as of non-adding the heirs of the 2nd party as well as claim of the objection filed against the inquiry report and then upon a concurrent finding thereto disallowing the revision upheld the judgment and order dated 1 23- 6-2011 as passed by the learned Additional Chief Judicial Magistrate, Bhola in MR Case No. 129 of 1973 for maintaining peace in holding actual possession of the 1st and 3rd party over the 216.12 acres of disputed land.
